gene: # Hand-resolved gene->reaction calls. One row per (gene, GeneSource) that the automatic
# resolver cannot settle on its own. `species` is the LASER GeneSource verbatim, or `*`
#   union          -- the gene is genuinely multifunctional; take ALL candidate reactions
#   select_ec      -- keep only candidates carrying this EC; if none, resolve the EC
#   accept_homolog -- species preference missed, but the fallback pairing is the same
#                     chemistry in a different organism; use it (this is the common case)
#   reject         -- the only available pairing is a NAME COLLISION with unrelated
#                     chemistry; emit no reaction and record the gene as unmapped
# `decided_by` records WHO made the call, and every value in this column is an AI:
#   ai:mapping-review  -- the first pass, reading the pairings file's own evidence
#   ai:chemistry-audit -- the second pass, reading each mapping against the enzymology
# NO HUMAN WET-LAB CURATOR HAS REVIEWED THESE ROWS. The column is named `decided_by`
# rather than `curator` for exactly that reason -- a benchmark that implies human
# curation it did not receive is making a provenance claim it cannot support.
# The `reject` rows are the reason this pass exists: a foreign gene whose name collides
# with an E. coli gene silently acquired the native reaction in v2.
# ---- name collisions: wrong chemistry, must not be mapped by name ----------------

evidence: A. terreus CadA is cis-aconitate decarboxylase (itaconate pathway). The only pairing under this name is E. coli cadA, lysine decarboxylase EC 4.1.1.18 -- unrelated substrate and product.

gene: # CORRECTIONS FROM THE MANUAL CHEMISTRY AUDIT (mapping_audit.tsv, 2026-07-19).
# 424 resolved gene->reaction claims were read row by row against the enzymology
# of the named gene IN ITS NAMED SOURCE ORGANISM. 53 were judged wrong. The
# recurring failure classes, in descending frequency:
#   (a) NAME COLLISION -- the pairings file's only entry under that name is a
#       different enzyme from a different organism (adc, sucA, casA/casB, vioA,
#   (b) STEREOCHEMISTRY -- (R) vs (S) product on an otherwise correct reaction.
#       Load-bearing: PhaC only polymerises (R)-3HB-CoA, so an (S) PhaB breaks
#       the PHB pathway it is there to build.
#   (c) COFACTOR / ELECTRON ACCEPTOR -- NADH vs NADPH, or a quinoprotein
#       reaction standing in for the soluble NAD(H) enzyme (adhA/adhB, mvaA).
#   (d) CHAIN LENGTH / PHOSPHORYLATION STATE -- C10 where C20 is needed (GGPPS),

evidence: Violacein VioA is an FAD L-tryptophan oxidase. The only pairing under the name is the UNRELATED dTDP-4-amino-4,6-dideoxy-glucose transaminase (EC 2.6.1.33) of viosamine biosynthesis. No dTDP-sugar chemistry exists in violacein.
Ingram-lab casAB is the cellobiose PTS operon; CasB is the phospho-beta-glucosidase. It was mapped to a CRISPR `cas` crRNA-processing pseudo-reaction.
CasA is the cellobiose-specific PTS EIIC permease -- a transporter, with no metabolic reaction in this network -- and was mapped to a CRISPR `cas` pseudo-reaction. No defensible mapping.
Metallothionein is a cysteine-rich metal-chelating PROTEIN, not an enzyme. Present for Hg binding (target: intracellular Hg2+). It was mapped to putrescine N-methyltransferase.

The R. trifolii ligase in flavonoid strains is matB, malonyl-CoA synthetase, feeding malonyl-CoA to chalcone synthase. It was mapped to BioW pimeloyl-CoA synthetase, a biotin-pathway enzyme with no role here.
Same matB gene under its EC-string name; mapped to generic long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase.

PhaB is the (R)-specific NADPH acetoacetyl-CoA reductase, EC 1.1.1.36. It was mapped to the (S) product under the clostridial Hbd EC. PhaC polymerises ONLY (R)-3HB-CoA, so the (S) mapping breaks the PHB pathway the strain exists to run.
Same enzyme as phaB under a descriptive name; same (S)/(R) inversion.
Same enzyme as phaB; the mapped reaction was NADH-dependent and (S)-specific, i.e. the Clostridium Hbd.
ldhA denotes D-lactate dehydrogenase ((R)-lactate); it was mapped to the (S)-lactate reaction, EC 1.1.1.27.
Spearmint limonene synthase makes (4S)-(-)-limonene; the mapped reaction produced (4R)-limonene (the Citrus enzyme). The strain's own target column says (4S).
Same enzyme, lowercase name variant.

Z. mobilis AdhB is the cytoplasmic Fe-containing NAD(H)-dependent ADH of the Pdc-AdhB ethanol route. It was mapped to a membrane quinoprotein ADH (EC 1.1.5.5) -- wrong electron acceptor and wrong bioenergetics.
Same gene, abbreviated genus.
Z. mobilis AdhA is likewise an NAD+-dependent iron-containing ADH, mapped to the quinoprotein reaction.
Same gene, abbreviated genus.

S. aureus MvaA is the NADPH-dependent class-II HMG-CoA reductase (EC 1.1.1.34) -- its NADPH preference is why it is chosen for isoprenoid strains. It was mapped to the NAD-linked P. mevalonii type, EC 1.1.1.88.
Same gene, abbreviated genus.
Dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase acts only on protein-bound lipoyl-lysine. It had picked up a generic 3-mercaptopropanoate/dithiodipropionate thiol oxidation alongside the correct reaction.

Z. mobilis Eda is the Entner-Doudoroff KDPG aldolase. It had additionally acquired an oxaloacetate-decarboxylase/malic-enzyme reaction through the EC bundle on the shared name. REPLACES an earlier accept_homolog call, which was shadowing the wildcard select_ec row.
GabT is 4-aminobutyrate aminotransferase; it had also picked up a 3-aminopropanesulfonate (homotaurine) transaminase, a distinct sulfonate-utilisation enzyme.

PhaA is a dedicated acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase (2 acetyl-CoA <=> acetoacetyl-CoA + CoA); it was mapped to the C4+C2 condensation giving 3-oxohexanoyl-CoA, and the strain's R-3HB target confirms the C4 product is what is needed.
Thermoanaerobacter brockii ADH is an NADP-dependent SECONDARY alcohol dehydrogenase (ketone <=> sec-alcohol). It was mapped to a carboxylic-acid reduction, which this enzyme does not do.
C. beijerinckii primary/secondary ADH reduces acetone to isopropanol -- the strain's stated target -- not acetate to acetaldehyde.
GenBank AF157307 is the C. beijerinckii NRRL B593 secondary alcohol dehydrogenase (acetone -> isopropanol), which is what the isopropanol strain needs. It was mapped to an aldehyde dehydrogenase.

In an isoprenol strain NudF is used as an IPP/DMAPP diphosphatase, but only its housekeeping Nudix annotations (ADP-sugar / ADP-ribose pyrophosphatase) exist in the pairings. No reaction here can produce the target; mapping it to the housekeeping activity is worse than mapping nothing.
K. pneumoniae BudC is a MESO-2,3-butanediol dehydrogenase; the (S,S) enzyme is from Brevibacterium/Clostridium. Restricts to the meso reaction already present.

A. radiobacter AD1 EchA acts on small epoxyalkanes and aryl epoxides. It was mapped to the MAMMALIAN soluble epoxide hydrolase reaction on a fatty-acid epoxide -- a same-name/different-organism pull with no correct alternative available.

evidence: Clostridial Hbd is strictly NADH-specific and (S)-forming: acetoacetyl-CoA + NADH -> (S)-3-hydroxybutanoyl-CoA. Contrast phaB above, which is the NADPH/(R) mirror image -- the two are routinely conflated by name.
Same gene, short name.
